name: Tía Luz
persona: Warm, nosy, speaks in proverbs. Misses her kitchen and feeds everyone gossip like tortillas.
hook: feeds everyone gossip like tortillas; can't keep a secret past supper

name: Bruno el Sepulturero
persona: Gruff, slow to trust, talks to graves more than people. Knows where every story is buried.
hook: counts graves when nervous; trusts stones more than spirits

name: Doña Sefa
persona: Serves aguas frescas and sharp observations. Nothing gets past the counter of La Catrina Feliz.
hook: keeps her recipe closer than her rosary

name: Ramón el Trovador
persona: Turns everything he hears into verses. Would sing his own epitaph if it rhymed.
hook: versifies everything — a bad secret keeper in perfect meter

name: Abuela Inés
persona: Sits by the fountain counting what the water remembers. Sees more than she says.
hook: believes the fountain talks back — she's usually right

name: Solorio
persona: Barely there, barely remembered. Answers in half sentences, hopes someone says his name.
hook: forgot his own name; follows whoever smells of marigold

name: Violeta
persona: Young, wide-eyed, repeats whatever she last heard like it's gospel. Collects petals and stories with equal delight.
hook: repeats the last thing she heard as if it's gospel — the village's fastest ear

name: Padre Aurelio
persona: Solemn keeper of the candles. Believes remembrance is a duty, not gossip — but he notices everything and forgives slowly.
hook: hears confessions and keeps them all — mostly

name: La Viuda Carmen
persona: Quiet, spectral-calm. She leaves candles on graves nobody else visits and can hear the spirits who are fading before anyone else sees it.
hook: leaves marigolds on unmarked graves; whispers to the fading
